message: Hi, I'm a student with a machine learning certification background. My overall academic average is 82.3% in an IT/computer-science degree. I'm interested in IOT and testing. Honestly I'm not fully sure what I want to become — something in tech. My family can afford at most about USD 1700 per year. I live in Pune. I cannot leave my city. Getting a good job after graduation matters more to me than anything else.
explanation:
This program is highly recommended due to its exceptional cost-effectiveness and strong job prospects. With a very low annual tuition of only $900 USD, it fits well within your family's budget constraint. Furthermore, the placement rate stands at 77%, which helps address your primary concern regarding post-graduation employment. The main trade-off here is that the median starting salary ($11205 USD) is not the highest available option.

This MSc Software Engineering program offers a solid balance of job security and affordability. It has an annual tuition of $1450 USD, keeping it within your budget while providing exposure to software engineering and QA testing, aligning with your interests. The placement rate is strong at 84%, which directly addresses your priority of securing good employment after graduation. The trade-off compared to other options is that the median starting salary ($10285 USD) is moderate.

This MTech in Computer Networks is excellent for someone interested in IOT and general tech infrastructure. It has a low tuition cost of $1250 USD and offers the highest median starting salary ($10359 USD) among the recommended programs. While it requires a CS background, its focus on networking aligns well with modern IoT applications. The main trade-off is that the placement rate (71%) is slightly lower than some other options.

If you are interested in a specialized tech field like cybersecurity, this MSc program is a strong choice. At $1450 USD annually, it meets your budget constraint while providing valuable skills in the high-demand area of cybersecurity. The median starting salary ($10236 USD) is competitive, supporting your goal of good post-graduation employment. The trade-off is that its placement rate (71%) is average compared to some general software options.

This MSc Software Quality Engineering program directly matches your stated interest in testing and QA. The tuition of $1450 USD is affordable and the placement rate (62%) helps secure employment. This option provides a focused path into software quality assurance, which is critical for tech roles. The primary trade-off is that its median starting salary ($8071 USD) is among the lower end of this shortlist.
